findings.quote:
def uri_to_iri(uri):
    """
    Convert a Uniform Resource Identifier(URI) into an Internationalized
    Resource Identifier(IRI).

    This is the algorithm from RFC 3987 Section 3.2, excluding step 4.

    Take an URI in ASCII bytes (e.g. '/I%20%E2%99%A5%20Django/') and return
    a string containing the encoded result (e.g. '/I%20♥%20Django/').
    """
    if uri is None:
        return uri
    uri = force_bytes(uri)
    # Fast selective unquote: First, split on '%' and then starting with the
    # second block, decode the first 2 bytes if they represent a hex code to
    # decode. The rest of the block is the part after '%AB', not containing
    # any '%'. Add that to the output without further processing.
    bits = uri.split(b"%")
    if len(bits) == 1:
        iri = uri
    else:
        parts = [bits[0]]
        append = parts.append
        hextobyte = _hextobyte
        for item in bits[1:]:
            hex = item[:2]
            if hex in hextobyte:
                append(hextobyte[item[:2]])
                append(item[2:])
            else:
                append(b"%")
                append(item)
        iri = b"".join(parts)
    return repercent_broken_unicode(iri).decode()
findings.explanation: The module-global target normalizes a non-`None` URI to bytes before selective percent-unquoting, repair/re-percenting of broken Unicode sequences, and final decoding to an IRI string. It uses default UTF-8, `strings_only=False`, and strict errors. `None` returns before the call; no conversion or final-decoding exception is handled locally.

if uri is None:
        return uri
    uri = force_bytes(uri)
    # Fast selective unquote: First, split on '%' and then starting with the
    # second block, decode the first 2 bytes if they represent a hex code to
    # decode. The rest of the block is the part after '%AB', not containing
    # any '%'. Add that to the output without further processing.
    bits = uri.split(b"%")
    if len(bits) == 1:
        iri = uri
    else:
        parts = [bits[0]]
        append = parts.append
        hextobyte = _hextobyte
        for item in bits[1:]:
            hex = item[:2]
            if hex in hextobyte:
                append(hextobyte[item[:2]])
                append(item[2:])
            else:
                append(b"%")
                append(item)
        iri = b"".join(parts)
    return repercent_broken_unicode(iri).decode()
findings.explanation: The same-module name is the requested force_bytes definition. It converts a non-None URI to bytes so the function can selectively decode percent-encoded byte sequences, re-percent malformed Unicode, and finally return a decoded IRI string. No options are supplied, so encoding is UTF-8, strings_only=False, and errors="strict". The None guard bypasses the lexical call at runtime; otherwise it is unconditional. There is no local exception handler for conversion or final decoding errors.
